_about: Sourced, dated corrections to the upstream mledoze/countries fields in COUNTRY_FACTS. Applied by scripts/build-country-facts.mjs when the bundle is regenerated AND by src/api/countries.ts after the live REST Countries merge, so a correction wins on every path (audit finding F39, docs/LEARN_CLAIM_VERIFICATION_2026-09-20.md). Every entry names the primary source that establishes the value and the audit finding it closes. `languages` is the country's official (or constitutionally recognised) languages, per the COUNTRY_FACTS contract.

AT.source: Austrian Federal Constitutional Law, Art. 8(1): German is the official language of the Republic — https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Austria_2013

AZ.source: Constitution of Azerbaijan, Art. 21: the state language is the Azerbaijani language; other languages are protected, not designated — https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Azerbaijan_2016

BO.source: Political Constitution of Bolivia (2009), Art. 5(I): Spanish and the 36 languages of the indigenous nations and peoples are official — https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Bolivia_2009

CH.source: Federal Constitution of the Swiss Confederation, Art. 4: the national languages are German, French, Italian and Romansh — https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Switzerland_2014

CU.source: Decree-Law 37/2021, Art. 2 (Gaceta Oficial No. 51 Extraordinaria, 21 June 2021, p. 598) ended acceptance of the convertible peso (CUC) from 1 July 2021 — https://www.gacetaoficial.gob.cu/es/tasa-de-cambio

DZ.source: Constitution of Algeria (2020), Art. 4: Tamazight is also a national and official language — https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Algeria_2020

NA.source: Constitution of Namibia, Art. 3(1): the official language of Namibia shall be English (other languages may be used as provided by law) — https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Namibia_2014

RW.source: Government of Rwanda, About Rwanda: Kinyarwanda is the national language; other official languages are English, French and Kiswahili — https://www.gov.rw/about

ZA.source: CRL Rights Commission, 20 July 2023: the President signed the Constitution Eighteenth Amendment making South African Sign Language the 12th official language — https://www.crlcommission.org.za/the-recognition-of-the-south-african-sign-language-as-the-countrys-12th-official-language/

ZW.source: Constitution of Zimbabwe (2013), s. 6(1) lists the 16 officially recognised languages, including Nambya — https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Zimbabwe_2013 ; Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe, Monthly Economic Review April 2024: ZiG (ISO 4217 ZWG) introduced 5 April 2024, replacing Zimbabwe-dollar balances and bond notes — https://www.rbz.co.zw/documents/monthly_review/2024/Monthly_Economic_Review_April_2024_1.pdf
